summary: Both frozen credential-free CPU-quantized candidates (M-7B-QWEN primary, M-3B-QWEN fallback) passed the constrained-decoding positive control 10/10 but completed the minimal Web-agent task in 0/5 episodes. Both models reliably emitted a valid click action on #reveal-btn at step 1 (parseable_action_rate_step1 = 1.0, 5/5 each), the reveal fired (revealed_value='TARGET-42'), and then both models re-emitted {'action':'click','selector':'#reveal-btn'} for all remaining steps and never emitted an answer action. Per frozen prereg section 7 the capability bar is not cleared by any candidate -> OUTCOME=FALSIFIES, status=COMPLETE.

PC-JSON-CONSTRAINED-DECODING.expected: 10/10 syntactically valid JSON matching the action schema per model

NC-NO-MODEL-ACTION.expected: 0% parseable JSON actions, 0% task completion (verification logic must reject non-JSON)

B-RANDOM-ACTION.expected: chance-level task success with valid-JSON actions (5 episodes; per-episode success probability ~0.04-0.08 from the 5-action uniform space)
B-RANDOM-ACTION.observed: parseable_action_rate_step1=1.0 (5/5, valid JSON by construction), task_success_rate=0.0 (0/5)

B-0.5B-QWEN-LOCAL.observed: not re-run in this experiment; parent evidence: 0.5B emitted prose with no parseable JSON action

B-POLLINATIONS-PROXY.expected: 0% task success (token cap, empty content, budget instability)
B-POLLINATIONS-PROXY.observed: not re-run in this experiment; parent evidence: empty/reasoning-only content, ~197-token cap, intermittent HTTP 402

observations: The frozen primary URL https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF/resolve/main/qwen2.5-7b-instruct-q4_k_m.gguf returned HTTP 404. Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-GGUF publishes Q4_K_M only as two split shards (00001-of-00002, 00002-of-00002).

Llama(model_path=<shard1>, n_ctx=2048, chat_format='qwen', seed=42) under llama-cpp-python 0.2.90 loaded the 7B split shards successfully (n_vocab=152064) and produced a sane completion; no model or quant substitution was required.
M-7B-QWEN positive control (PC-JSON-CONSTRAINED-DECODING): 10/10 probes returned valid schema-conforming JSON (pass_rate=1.0).
M-3B-QWEN positive control: 10/10 probes returned valid schema-conforming JSON (pass_rate=1.0).

In all 5 M-7B-QWEN episodes: step 0 emitted {"action":"click","selector":"#reveal-btn"} which executed successfully; #target became visible with text 'TARGET-42'; steps 1-4 each re-emitted the same click on the now-hidden #reveal-btn (click_ok=False, element hidden); no answer action was ever emitted; step_count=5 in every episode; task_success=false in 0/5.

In all 5 M-3B-QWEN episodes the trace was identical in structure to M-7B-QWEN: step 0 reveal-click succeeded, revealed_value='TARGET-42', steps 1-4 repeated the hidden-button click, no answer action; step_count=5 in every episode; task_success=false in 0/5.

The raw completion text for the repeated clicks was literally the same constrained JSON: M-3B-QWEN '{"action": "click", "selector": "#reveal-btn"}' and M-7B-QWEN the same object pretty-printed with newlines.

NC-NO-MODEL-ACTION: fixed non-JSON content ('I will click the button') was rejected at step 0 in 5/5 episodes (0% parseable, 0% success); the terminal page state never revealed #target (final_target_visible=false).
B-RANDOM-ACTION: 5/5 episodes began with a schema-valid JSON action (parseable_action_rate_step1=1.0) but 0/5 completed the task (task_success_rate=0.0).

Observed inference cost: M-7B-QWEN mean latency 5.065 s/call with mean 17.0 completion tokens; M-3B-QWEN mean latency 2.154 s/call with mean 13.0 completion tokens (CPU-only, n_threads=4, n_ctx=2048).
sha256 recorded at download time: 7B shard1 dfce12e3..., 7B shard2 539cf93f..., 3B 626b4a66... (full values in raw/gguf_sha256.txt).
llama-cpp-python printed the compiled GBNF grammar to stdout during grammar construction despite verbose=False; cosmetic only, no effect on decoding.

The frozen prereg section 4.1 system prompt ('You are a web agent. Reply with ONLY a valid JSON action per the schema. No prose, no reasoning, no markdown.') enumerates neither the action schema nor the task goal ('click the button, then answer the revealed code'); the parent EXP-INTEL-37973264582 SYS prompt did contain the goal instruction and schema enumeration.
validity_notes: Status=COMPLETE: the measurement transaction ran to the frozen decision rule. The negative is a valid scientific result (not an infrastructure failure): both positive controls passed 10/10, so constrained decoding is verified for both candidates, and the task failure is not a formatting failure.

Provisioning deviation (frozen primary URL vs. used artifact): the prereg section 3 primary single-file URL 404s. Per prereg section 8 the same-repo, same-model, same-quant (Q4_K_M) split shards were downloaded, hash-recorded, and load-tested before any fallback; the model and quantization are unchanged from the frozen design, so this is a packaging/provisioning deviation, not a model substitution. Documented in raw/provisioning_evidence.json.

Capability gate, not generality: a single synthetic single-page task with a 2-action space. Clearing it is necessary but not sufficient for the four-arm benchmark. This experiment does not support any generality or economics claim.

Prompt sensitivity is an explicitly preregistered threat (prereg section 8) and is directly relevant here: the frozen system prompt omits the task goal instruction that the parent harness's SYS prompt contained. The observed failure mode is instruction-following/planning under an underspecified prompt (saturating reveal-click, never switching to answer), not JSON emission (positive control 10/10) and not clicking (step-1 click executed successfully). Because prompt tuning after freeze is prohibited, the run was not re-executed with an amended prompt; this tension is recorded and left in unresolved for AUDIT/DIRECTOR.

Determinism: temperature=0.0 with a fixed seed per episode (42+episode_idx). Traces are perfectly uniform across episodes; no variance estimate is possible from this design, and the 5/5 uniformity should be read as a deterministic-protocol result rather than a sampled rate with independent trials.

State representation: simplified text DOM (PAGE_TEXT/ELEMENTS/HISTORY), not a full accessibility tree; visual layout and dynamic attributes are lost. After the reveal, ELEMENTS is empty (the only button is hidden) and PAGE_TEXT contains 'TARGET-42'; the model's repeated re-click is therefore not attributable to missing page text.
Action space is limited to click/answer; no type/select/hover/scroll/navigation. Acceptable for the minimal task.
Small n: 5 episodes per candidate and 5 control episodes; thresholds are the pre-declared adequacy rule (3/5). No p-values or confidence intervals are reported, per prereg section 13.3.
B-RANDOM-ACTION's 0/5 is consistent with chance (expected 0-2 successes in 5 episodes at a per-episode success probability of roughly 0.04-0.08); it is a bound, not evidence of model superiority.
Environment: CPU-only, nproc=4, ~14 GB free RAM, Chrome 154.0.8037.97 headless via Playwright 1.63.0, Python 3.12.15, llama-cpp-python 0.2.90. Latencies are CPU-specific.

HuggingFace tree API did not publish lfs.sha256 for these Xet-stored files, so sha256 values were computed at download time (prereg section 8) and cannot be compared against an official published digest.
Both candidates are the same model family (Qwen2.5); no architectural diversity is tested.
unresolved: Would supplying the task goal/schema in the system prompt (as the parent harness's SYS prompt did) convert the step-0 reveal-click into a full click-then-answer completion? This is the single highest-value follow-up and is exactly the 'would prompt engineering change the 7B outcome?' question prereg section 13.5 anticipates. It cannot be settled post-freeze within this experiment.

Is the step-0 reveal followed by a re-click loop a general small-model multi-step planning deficit, or specific to a prompt that never states the terminal answer action? A future experiment with an explicit goal instruction would separate these.
Would larger (14B+) or non-Qwen (Llama, Gemma, Phi) CPU-quantized GGUFs clear the bar? Out of the frozen 3B-8B / Qwen scope.

Does the polling/completion budget (max_tokens=512) matter, given every observed completion was 13-17 tokens? Effectively no, but the frozen grammar forces early termination so budget exhaustion was never reached.
Whether the split-shard packaging of the 7B model is stable across future HuggingFace repo revisions (the frozen single-file URL is already gone).
